name: libbs2b
why: Crossfeed DSP that turns stereo into a more natural headphone soundstage, a neat audio idea nobody knows about.

brief.what_it_is: libbs2b is a C library and set of plugins implementing the Bauer stereophonic-to-binaural DSP (bs2b), a crossfeed filter for headphone listening. It takes a stereo audio signal and mixes a filtered, delayed copy of each channel into the opposite channel, with a low-pass filter and a high-boost filter, so the sound seems less like it is inside the head. The homepage describes single-pole recursive digital filters with a fixed time delay to the far ear. The Brew formula installs two command-line tools, bs2bconvert and bs2bstream, but the homepage does not document them. The SourceForge page lists Windows, Mac, Linux, BSD and ChromeOS, and mentions Winamp and foobar2000 plugins in user reviews.
brief.why_it_exists: The author's preface argues that stereo records are mixed for loudspeakers, so long headphone listening causes fatigue from a 'superstereo' effect. What headphones lack is the sound from each channel reaching the opposite ear a little later and with some high-frequency roll-off from head shadowing. bs2b is meant to supply that missing crossfeed cheaply in digital form.
brief.how_it_works: The DSP is built from single-pole recursive filters, with the recursion O[n] = a0 * I[n] + a1 * I[n-1] + b1 * O[n-1]. The author says these behave like RC analog filters, which avoids the comb-filter artifacts he associates with FFT-based crossfeed. The low-pass and high-boost cutoffs are chosen so the crossfeed delay and frequency response come out smooth. The page says it does not simulate ambience and does not apply an HRTF at high frequencies.

commands_seen.context: Example from the Theory section's Perl script comments, labelled 'Default preset (700Hz, 4.5dB)'. It prints the filter's frequency and delay response for the given low-pass cutoff, low-pass gain in dB, and high-boost gain in dB.
Example from the same script comments, labelled 'Chu Moy's preset (700Hz, 6.0dB)'.

brief.install_notes: The homepage has no install or build instructions. The SourceForge page offers downloads per platform and a Winamp plugin file, and user reviews describe placing the Winamp DSP in AIMP's plugins folder. Running the theory script needs Perl with Math::Complex. The Brew formula's executables are bs2bconvert and bs2bstream, but I did not see their usage on the pages I read.
brief.standout: It is a small, documented DSP built on a few one-pole filters with presets tied to named crossfeed designs from Bauer, Chu Moy and Jan Meier. The homepage includes the Perl script that computes the response, so the filter math can be checked directly.
brief.status: Maintained, with weak evidence. The SourceForge project page shows Last Update 2024-10-23 and registration in 2005. I did not check a commit history or a changelog, and the homepage itself has no release notes or date.
brief.caveats: The homepage does not document the bs2bconvert or bs2bstream command-line usage, so the entry should not describe their options. The homepage has no build instructions and no licence statement. The SourceForge page lists GPLv2 and MIT, so check the licence in the source before relying on it. The author says the design gives no ambience simulation and no high-frequency HRTF. The SourceForge reviews are from 2012 to 2018 and mention only Windows players.
quotes: The Bauer stereophonic-to-binaural DSP (bs2b) library and plugins is designed to improve headphone listening of stereo audio records.
Plug in your headphones and try to feel sound little out from your head.
